Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the one-pager — helpful. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing internally: 

- For the PoC we prefer a Private VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC) but we understand Dedicated could be a short-term option if there are timing constraints. The primary requirement is that customer data (inference inputs and outputs) and logs remain in our VPC; we cannot have model weights or raw user data stored in a shared Redwood-managed environment without a stronger contractual agreement.
- We need assurance around encryption in transit and at rest (KMS integration), plus the ability to rotate keys.
- Audit log access: we need immutable logs and the ability to export them to our SIEM.
- Timeline: ideally PoC kickoff within 4–6 weeks. Can you confirm estimated setup time for Private VPC vs Dedicated?

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the detail — that aligns with what we heard. High-level answers here and proposed plan: 

1) Private VPC vs Dedicated (short):
   - Private VPC: customer-managed networking (VPC peering or AWS Transit Gateway), no egress of logs or artifacts to Redwood-managed storage by default, KMS integration with customer keys, option to host model artifacts in your subnet for on-premlike isolation. This is our recommended path for regulated workloads.
   - Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity in a Redwood-managed network. Dedicated gives throughput guarantees but the runtime and some operational artifacts remain on Redwood-managed infra; logs and metrics can be forwarded to your SIEM but model artifacts are hosted by Redwood unless we agree to a separately provisioned approach.

2) Timeline: Private VPC PoC: typically 4–6 weeks from contract + network prep; Dedicated PoC can be 2–3 weeks. Final timeline depends on network approvals and KMS onboarding.

3) Compliance/evidence: attaching a SOC 2 summary and will provide SOC 2 attestation over NDA.

Next steps:
- Mateo, can we get a short list of ports/peering requirements and an estimated timeline for a Private VPC PoC?
- Alice, if you can share a single network contact or preferred times, we’ll schedule the deep-dive for Wed/Thu.

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation expectations (technical follow-up)

Hi Alice / Marissa —

Thanks for looping me in. A few technical specifics to help your network/security team evaluate Private VPC: 

Network & isolation model:
- VPC peering or Transit Gateway supported (AWS example); for on-prem we can support an appliance or private link.
- All inference traffic can be restricted to the peered connection; no internet egress required.

Artifacts & model weights:
- By default our hosted model weights are stored in Redwood-managed storage. For Private VPC we offer options:
  1) Host model weights in a customer subnet (requires additional ops work and contractual terms).
  2) Use Redwood-hosted weights but enforce strict access controls and contractual restrictions — simpler but less isolated.
- We do not train on customer data unless explicitly contracted.

Encryption & keys:
- KMS integration (customer-managed keys) supported for data at rest; TLS 1.2+ in transit. We also support HSM-based key stores for high assurance customers.

Logging & audit:
- Audit logs can be exported to your S3 or pushed to your SIEM (syslog/forwarder). Immutable retention policies can be configured on your side.

Operational ask for sizing and timeline:
- QPS expectations (avg and peak), typical prompt length (max tokens), and desired P99 latency SLO.
- For PoC we typically need 1–2 weeks of infra prep after network peering + 2–4 weeks of deployment/config and testing (total 4–6 weeks).

Ports/Endpoints (AWS example):
- Allow outbound to 10.0.0.0/16 (Redwood pod subnet) over TCP 443 for control plane (if using peering) OR set up private link endpoints.
- Specific port list and CIDR will be provided in the network prep doc.

Happy to join the tech deep-dive — propose Wed 11:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
